summary: One tiny correction: in the smith's words, 'turn on, turn on' is followed by a semicolon in every edition of Franklin I checked, not a colon. Everything else checked out, including Franklin's other quotations, the Seneca passage, all three studies and every link.

changes.before: turn on, turn on: we shall have it bright
changes.after: turn on, turn on; we shall have it bright
changes.why: Misquotation: the published text of Franklin's Autobiography has a semicolon here, not a colon.

notes: Franklin's quotations follow the modernised 19th-century editions (as on ushistory.org and Project Gutenberg), not his manuscript spelling. That is fine; the wording matches a published text.

The Harkin meta-analysis appeared online in October 2015 and in print in 2016; the Etkin study was publicised in December 2015 and printed in the Journal of Consumer Research in April 2016. '2016' is right for both.
The Seneca passage is paraphrased, not quoted, and matches published translations of On Anger, Book Three, chapter 36.
The ushistory.org page for the speckled axe has a typing slip ('apeckled ax'); the story's 'speckled ax' matches the other editions.

history.summary: Published before the fact-checker existed. Waiting for its first check.
